title: Guía del Participante de 100Mi Patagonia Run 2026 — official participant guide
claims: The official 2026 100Mi Participant Guide is a 24-page PDF titled 'Guía del Participante de 100Mi Patagonia Run 2026'; it gives 160.3 km, +9,221 m, an approximate maximum altitude of 1,959 m, three summits, a 42-hour limit and a finish closing at 08:00 on Sunday 12 April 2026.

The guide's PAS table lists 20 rows with distance from the start and cumulative D+: Vallescondido 1 5.3 km/363 m, Galpón 13.1/1,037, Las Pendientes 22.4/1,888, Maderero 36/2,870, Vallescondido 2 48.3/3,353, Gimnasio 52.5/3,406, PAEX 1 52.5, Rosales 61/3,964, Portezuelo 67.9/4,607, Colorado 1 78.2/5,186, Mallín 88.5/5,864, Quechuquina 104.7/6,392, Nonthue 111.1/6,667, PAEX 2 111.1/6,667, Lago 121.8/6,941, Cohíue 130/7,791, Colorado 2 142.4/8,558, Bayos 151/8,730, Ruta 48 152.8 and finish 160.3/9,221.

The 2026 guide gives eight intermediate cut-offs plus the finish: Gimnasio/PAEX 1 at 02:00 Saturday, Quechuquina at 20:00 Saturday, Nonthue/PAEX 2 at 21:00 Saturday, Lago at 23:15 Saturday, Cohíue at 02:00 Sunday, Colorado 2 at 05:00 Sunday, Bayos at 06:00 Sunday, Ruta 48 at 06:30 Sunday and the finish at 08:00 Sunday; these are clock times, not elapsed race times.
The guide lists three PAS Total - Gimnasio, Colorado and Nonthue - and two PAEx at km 52.5 and km 111.1.

Mandatory kit in the 2026 guide includes two headlamps of at least 200 lumens each with batteries for 30 hours, an emergency whistle, a survival blanket, at least 1.5 litres of water capacity, a personal cup, a ziplock bag for rubbish and warm clothing; disposable cups are not provided.
The guide states that GPS tracks are not shared and that private or restricted land is authorised only for and during the event.
The 2026 race starts on Friday 10 April at 14:00 from RCM4; the finish closes at Plaza San Martín at 08:00 on Sunday 12 April and the awards are at 11:00.
The guide includes a full 2026 elevation profile and partial profiles by PAS, but no route map or GPS track.
